why_relevant: Positions itself as a Ukrainian fintech startup with its own banking licence; a small challenger where a single product-lead hire is materially informative.

source_name: Банк Власний Рахунок — official Facebook page
why_relevant: This small bank publishes team-focused content ('Про неймовірну команду...') on Facebook rather than via a press wire; for such actors social is the primary org-change channel.
Cheap, footnoted baseline for the actor map: corporate structure, founder roles, headcount figures (800+ employees, Feb 2026) and citation trails to primary sources. Not a signal source itself.

source_name: tgstat.com — Telegram channel analytics for UA fintech/founder channels
why_relevant: Gives searchable post archives, posting-frequency and audience metrics for founder and jobs channels — useful for backfilling history and for discovering adjacent neobank/HR channels.

Anonymous-candidate job marketplace dominant in UA tech; its monthly market analytics give the denominator (candidates per vacancy) needed to tell 'neobank is expanding' from 'whole market is hiring'.

source_name: minfin.com.ua — company cards for izibank and UA banks
why_relevant: Consumer-finance portal with per-institution cards (licence, МФО, ЄДРПОУ, news, reviews); a convenient entity-resolution layer linking neobank brands to their licensed banks.

source_name: Work.ua — Finance & banking vacancy category (Фінанси, банк)
why_relevant: Ukraine's largest general job board; the 'Фінанси, банк' rubric is the single densest stream of banking vacancy postings in UA. Category listing pages show a running vacancy count (search snippet indicated ~4,373 open finance/banking jobs), which makes vacancy-volume time series trivially derivable. Job titles reveal new role types (Head of Open Banking, еквайринг, ризик-менеджер) and city fields reveal hiring-location shifts (Kyiv vs Lviv vs remote/віддалено).

source_name: Work.ua — keyword vacancy search (title-level queries: еквайринг, платіжні системи, комплаєнс)
why_relevant: Keyword-scoped search URLs are the mechanism for the leading-indicator signal: counting how many postings mention еквайринг / POS / процесинг / Open Banking / PSD2 / AML over time exposes restructuring before it is announced. URL pattern is stable and query-parameterisable.
Reverse signal: a spike of CVs from a given bank's branch managers or acquiring staff indicates layoffs/branch closures before any press release. Complements the vacancy stream.

Work.ua publishes trend/forecast pieces built on its own vacancy database (e.g. 2026 labour-market trends). Gives a validated baseline against which our own counts can be sanity-checked, plus sector breakdowns we cannot compute ourselves.

The other half of the UA general job-board duopoly. Bank employer profiles on robota.ua carry structured company pages, so vacancy postings can be attributed to a specific bank and tracked per employer — essential for detecting one bank scaling an acquiring or IT team.
Company/press page linking to robota.ua's press releases, datasets, partnerships and API/product notes; a route to formal data-access requests rather than scraping.

Dominant CEE tech-talent marketplace. Its finance category is where Ukrainian banks and PSPs post engineering/product roles that never appear on work.ua. Company-scoped URLs exist (monobank/Fintech Band, OTP Bank UA), so per-bank tech-hiring volume is directly measurable — the cleanest proxy for digital/payments platform investment.

Monthly quantitative analytics on the Ukrainian tech job market (vacancy counts, applications-per-vacancy, salary bands) derived from Djinni's own database. Gives market-wide denominators so a bank's hiring surge can be normalised against sector-wide movement.

DOU is the reference IT-community site in Ukraine; its vacancy search has an explicit query-string parameter (?search=), making keyword-based vacancy-volume tracking straightforward (bank, платежі, payments, acquiring, fintech).

source_name: DOU.ua — company vacancy pages for banks/fintechs (mono, ПриватБанк, Djinni etc.)
why_relevant: Per-employer vacancy pages give a clean, attributable hiring series per institution, plus a company profile page with headcount, offices and reviews. PrivatBank and mono (monobank/Fintech Band) are the two largest UA banking tech employers; their DOU pages are the best single-employer hiring gauges available.

Cross-board aggregator (67 countries) that pulls postings from many UA sources including small/regional boards and employer sites we would otherwise miss. Its query pages carry an explicit vacancy count in the page title (e.g. 'Банк Київ — 927 актуальних вакансій'), making it a cheap volume index; city-scoped URL slugs support hiring-location-shift tracking down to small towns (e.g. Бровари).

source_name: LinkedIn Jobs — Ukraine, banking & payments filters
why_relevant: The only board where senior/executive banking roles in UA are reliably posted in English (Head of, Chief, Director), and where international banks (Raiffeisen, OTP, Piraeus, Citi) post. Also the only source where an individual leadership move (title change on a profile) is visible — the single most direct signal for the 'leadership moves' topic.

Surfaced repeatedly as a search-indexed proxy for English-language Ukraine roles that LinkedIn hides; a concrete find in results was Piraeus Bank Ukraine recruiting a Head of Business Intelligence — exactly the leading-indicator role type this cell targets. Also carries employer reviews that hint at reorganisation.

source_name: GRC.UA — job portal for experienced/senior candidates
why_relevant: Positions itself for 'talented and experienced' candidates and international/large Ukrainian employers — i.e. skewed toward the managerial and specialist banking roles our cell cares about, rather than mass-market retail vacancies. Third distinct posting pool after work.ua and robota.ua.

Second aggregator (search snippet indicated ~37.7k UA vacancies) that collects postings from multiple sources into one place; useful as a redundancy/dedup cross-check against Jooble and for salary-statistics pages it publishes per job title.

Curated career platform with an explicit FinTech/Finance category filter and structured company pages (e.g. Alfa-Bank Ukraine / Sense Bank, Ministry of Finance). Smaller volume but higher signal-to-noise for white-collar and newly created role types; company pages act as an actor map.

source_name: data.gov.ua — State Employment Service datasets (form 3-ПН vacancies)
why_relevant: Machine-readable, legally open datasets of employer-submitted vacancies (reporting form 3-ПН). This is the only fully licence-clean bulk vacancy source in the cell — no ToS risk, structured, and includes occupation classifier codes that let us isolate financial/banking occupations and their regional distribution over time.

source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — recruiting / vacancies page
why_relevant: The regulator's own hiring is a first-order org-change signal: a vacancy such as 'Спеціаліст по роботі з учасниками платіжного ринку' (specialist for work with payment market participants) telegraphs where NBU is expanding supervisory capacity — i.e. which part of the payments market is about to be regulated harder. Highest-credibility employer source in the cell.

Ukraine's largest bank (~a quarter of the banking system) runs its own ATS/career portal. First-party postings appear here before or instead of aggregators, and internship/graduate programmes signal planned headcount growth. Branch-level vacancy geography is the sharpest available proxy for branch network expansion or contraction.

source_name: Bank & PSP own career pages (Accordbank, PSP Platon, and peers)
why_relevant: Mid-size banks and payment service providers publish vacancies only on their own sites, and these are precisely the institutions where a single new role (e.g. an acquiring or Open Banking lead) is materially informative. Platon's career page confirms PSPs use this channel too. Building a roster of such pages closes the long tail the big boards miss.

A sector-specific vertical: banking vacancies collected on a banking portal rather than a general board. Narrow but pre-filtered to exactly our sector, so it needs no classification step and is a useful recall check on whether our keyword filters on work.ua/robota.ua are missing postings.
